## Executive summary

I was the business-side owner of a purchase-prediction model for ad targeting. I turned campaign objectives into model requirements and designed the experiment that tested its commercial value, so decisions rested on more than an offline score.

## Business challenge

LINE's advertising business had an opportunity to help brands reach users who are more likely to buy. Better targeting means better campaign returns for advertisers and more ad spend on the platform.

The data science team could build a purchase-prediction model. What was missing was a way to **turn campaign objectives into model requirements**, and to test whether the model created real commercial value.

## My role

The data science team built and validated the model; I owned what it should do and how we would judge it.

::: {.compare}
::: {.after}
[Business / Product (my role)]{.compare-title}

- Problem framing and success metrics
- Customer and campaign context
- Business input into the model's requirements
- Prioritizing where to pilot
- Experiment design
- Business evaluation of the results
:::
::: {}
[Data Science team]{.compare-title}

- Feature engineering
- Model development
- Model validation
- Scoring output generation
:::
:::

The two sides worked closely at the boundary, and I made sure model scores came out in a form sales and account teams could use directly.

## Analytical approach

A model that scores well offline doesn't always move campaign results. I designed the test to **isolate the effect of the new targeting approach** from everything else in the campaign, using random assignment against a control group.

## Illustrative decision framework

**How the experiment turns into a decision**

[Illustrative framework]{.provenance .provenance-illustrative}

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A[Eligible audience for pilot campaigns] --> B{Random assignment}
    B --> C[Control: existing targeting]
    B --> D[Treatment: model-based segments]
    C --> E[Compare campaign metrics]
    D --> E
    E --> F[Statistical check and business read-out]
    F --> G[Scale-up decision]
```

[Illustrative framework: a generic A/B test design. It does not show LINE's actual audiences, targeting signals, or results.]{.illustrative}

## Outcome

- Pilot campaigns using the new targeting segments performed well against the control group
- The results **informed campaign investment decisions** for model-based targeting

## Lessons learned

- **Offline scores aren't the finish line.** A controlled test shows whether a model changes campaign results.
- **Decide how you'll judge success first.** Agreeing on metrics up front makes the read-out easier to act on.
- **Design for the end user.** Scores only help if sales and account teams can use them directly.

## Skills & methods

Experiment design · A/B testing and incrementality · translating business goals into ML requirements · campaign performance measurement · cross-functional partnership with data science
